citations.quote:
Put $K=\mathbb Q(q)$, $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, $p=q+q^{-1}$ and $h=q^2+q^{-2}$. For $k\ge0$ set

$$n_{2k}=8k+2,\qquad n_{2k+1}=8k+4,\qquad \ell_{2k}=2,\qquad\ell_{2k+1}=4,\qquad r_j=\ell_j-1,$$

and set $p_j=p$ for even $j$ and $p_j=h$ for odd $j$. Let $u_{j,a}=F^{(a)}u_{j,0}$, $0\le a\le n_j$, be the divided basis of the highest string $V(n_j)$, of weight $n_j-2a$. On the algebraic module $M=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}V(n_j)$ define

$$T_j u_{j,t\ell_j}=(-1)^t u_{j+1,r_j+t\ell_j}\quad(0\le t\le n_j/\ell_j),$$

and define $T_j$ to be zero on all other divided basis vectors. Put $S=\sum_jT_j/p_j$, $C=1+S$, and $b_{j,a}=C u_{j,a}$.

Then $S^2=0$ and $C^{-1}=1-S$; these are finite-column algebraic operators. The homogeneous basis $B=\{b_{j,a}\}$ has a free $U_A$-stable integral span, its standard compatible bar fixes $B$, and its regular zero and infinity charts and crystal residues are those of the standard direct sum of divided strings. Thus it is an actual four-axiom based integrable finite-Cartan-type module, with a balanced integral triple and no choice assumption.

For every $J\ge0$, the finite version $M^{(J)}=\bigoplus_{0\le j\le J}V(n_j)$, with shears only for $j<J$, has the same properties. For every $a\in U_A$ the raw-coordinate action is $C^{-1}aC=a+[a,S]-SaS$; its column at a raw basis vector of index $j$ is supported at summand indices at most $j+2$. That column agrees with the finite version whenever $J\ge j+2$.

The raw seed $b_{0,0}\otimes b_{0,2}$ in two copies has total weight zero and factor weights $2,-2$. Both factors are deformed: $b_{0,0}=u_{0,0}+u_{1,1}/p$ and $b_{0,2}=u_{0,2}-u_{1,3}/p$. This statement constructs the modules and finite versions; it does not assert infinite tensor correction supports.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

In the same positive-first/negative-second completion $\widehat C$ of [[def-root-height-completion-for-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiners]], let $\Theta=\sum_\nu\Theta_\nu$ be the unique normalized bar-coproduct intertwiner of [[thm-the-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiner-exists-and-is-unique]]. Then:

(i) $\Theta^{-1}=\overline\Theta=(\psi\otimes\psi)(\Theta)$, the inverse being taken in the root-height convolution algebra of $\widehat C$ and not switching the positive and negative tensor order;

(ii) for every $\nu$ the exact threefold identities hold:
$$(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{23}(1\otimes K_{-\eta}\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{13},$$
$$(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{12}(1\otimes K_\eta\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{13},$$
with subscripts denoting tensor positions and $\Theta_{\nu'}=0$ when $\nu'\notin Q_+$;

(iii) the two normalized tensor-bar compositions satisfy the field cocycle identity
$$((\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Theta)\Theta_{12}=((\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Theta)\Theta_{23},$$
coefficientwise in the transported source completion and on every vector for which the iterated actions are finite;

(iv) the bar-coproduct counterpart needed for the cocycle is
$$(\mathrm{id}\otimes\overline\Delta)\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{13}(1\otimes K_{-\gamma}\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{12}.$$

Removing the normalization $\Theta_0=1$ permits arbitrary scalar multiples of the same linear intertwiner equation, so normalization is essential for uniqueness; no integrality of coefficients and no uncontrolled infinite evaluation is asserted.

derivations.claim: **Finite cuts and their correction.** In a finite cut every evaluated degree is bounded by the finite divided strings, and [F2] is a finite sum of integral divided actions. Thus $\Psi_J$ is an integral semilinear involution. Degree zero is the identity, while degree $r>0$ raises first weight by $2r$. Finite first-weight induction constructs the corrected seed: at the next weight its residual is anti-bar by involutivity, so [F3] supplies its unique positive-polynomial correction. There are only finitely many raw vectors and weights in the cut, hence this process terminates. If two normalized fixed lifts differed, the coefficients at the least first weight of their difference would be in $q\mathbb Z[q]$ and equal their own bars, hence zero. This proves existence and uniqueness without an infinite completion.

**Projection coherence, including the cutoff.** Let $P_J$ keep raw tensor coordinates with both constituent indices at most $J$ and map them to the corresponding cut raw basis. To calculate a raw bar column, expand by $C\otimes C$, apply [F2], and reexpress by $C^{-1}\otimes C^{-1}$. All nonidentity expansion and reexpression terms increase a constituent index, and the middle operator preserves both indices. A term using the omitted outgoing shear at index $J$ is outside the retained rectangle and cannot return. An input outside that rectangle likewise cannot return. The retained raw columns are consequently exactly the cut columns, giving $P_J\Psi_L=\Psi_JP_J$ for $L\ge J$ and also $P_J\Psi=\Psi_JP_J$ for the algebraic full module. Since $P_J$ preserves the seed, weights and polynomial correction coefficients, step 1.1 gives $P_Jg^{(L)}=g^{(J)}$. This proves endpoint independence at the actual deleted-last-shear boundary.

**Four states and three transfer bands.** Work at total weight zero, and use first position $a$ and second bottom-distance $d$. The seed has $(a,d)=(0,0)$. On $0\le a,d\le3$, even shears send offsets $0\mapsto1$ and $2\mapsto3$, odd shears send only $0\mapsto3$, and inverse shears have the same supports. Degree $r$ decreases both offsets by $r$. Thus all reached raw coordinates remain in this envelope and $r\le3$. At first weight $2+2t$, both factors satisfy $n_j/2-a=t+1$ or $n_l/2-d=t+1$. For $t=4k+s$, $s=0,1,2,3$, the two possibilities are respectively $((2k,0),(2k+1,1))$, $((2k+1,0),(2k+2,3))$, $((2k+2,2),(2k+3,3))$, and $((2k+2,1),(2k+3,2))$. Order their tensor pairs $LL,LH,HL,HH$. Let $B_{t,r}$ be the four-by-four raw coefficient matrix from layer $t$ to $t+r$, obtained by the three finite operations of step 2.1. Then $B_{t,0}=I$ and there are no bands beyond $r=3$. The coefficient family $f_0=(1,0,0,0)^T$, $f_t=\mathcal P(\sum_{r=1}^{\min(3,t)}B_{t-r,r}\bar f_{t-r})$ is well defined layer by layer: each partial sum is a finite algebraic vector, its least unsolved residual is anti-bar, and the integral full bar makes that residual Laurent. No infinite vector is asserted to belong to the module. The symmetry of the shear signs and the two Gaussian factors in [F2] preserves $f_t=(P,Q,-Q,R)^T$.

**The scalar passed between four-layer cycles.** At layer $4k+1$, standard constituent $2k+2$ first appears, at offsets $(3,3)$, with coefficient $c_k=-(P-2hQ-h^2R)/h^2$. This follows by expanding the four raw states: the lower constituent is odd, its first top shear has coefficient $1/h$, and its second bottom shear has coefficient $-1/h$. Earlier layers cannot enter constituent $2k+2$, because odd shears require offset zero and that first occurs at this layer. At this point a future residual with an old first constituent is impossible above its top weight; a mixed new/old constituent term has an old second bottom or an old first top, so its positive quasi-$R$ terms vanish. The only remaining future residual is therefore $c_k(\Psi v_{2k+2,3;2k+2,3}-v_{2k+2,3;2k+2,3})$. Its initial center coefficient is bar fixed, since no earlier standard coordinate in this diagonal constituent can contribute to its first weight. Consequently the next four-layer correction depends only on $c_k$. Positive-part extraction is linear over $\mathbb Q$ (and over $\mathbb Z$ on integral coefficients); no linearity over $\mathbb Q(q)$ is claimed. In the induction below only the integer scalar $a_k$ is taken outside it. At $k=0$, [F2] gives $f_1=(-q^5+q^3-2q,-q^3+q,q^3-q,q)^T$, so $P-2hQ-h^2R=-p(h+1)$.

**Explicit matrices and integral ghost residual.** Let $E_{21}$ be the two-by-two matrix with its only nonzero entry $1$ at $(2,1)$, and put $D_t=(I+\alpha_tE_{21})\otimes(I-\alpha_tE_{21})$, with $\alpha_t=1/p,1/h,-1/p,0$ according as $t\bmod4=0,1,2,3$. This is exactly $C\otimes C$ between the four raw and standard states of step 3.1. For a source factor state $(j,a)$ and a target state $(j,a-r)$, put $\gamma(j,a,r)=\binom{n_j-a+r}{r}_q$; put the entry zero if that same constituent target is absent. Define $T_{t,r}$ on tensor pairs by $A_r\gamma(j,a,r)\gamma(l,d,r)$ in the matching target pair and zero elsewhere. Then the completely specified four-by-four matrices are $B_{t,r}=D_{t+r}^{-1}T_{t,r}D_t$. This includes $B_{t,0}=I$. For the diagonal ghost in step 4.1 the new string has $n=8k+10$, and its three positive divided coefficients are $G_r=\binom{8k+7+r}{r}_q$, $r=1,2,3$. Each $G_r$ is divisible by $h$: the upper and lower remainders modulo $4$ are respectively $(0,1),(1,2),(2,3)$, so the Gaussian block argument proved in the construction gives zero modulo $h$. Likewise $p\mid G_1,G_3$ by their upper/lower remainders modulo $2$. Thus $h^2\mid G_r^2$ for all three degrees, and $p^2h^2\mid G_r^2$ for degrees $1,3$. Reexpressing the resulting standard offset $3-r$ uses no shear for $r=2$, and at most the two denominators $p$ for $r=1,3$. Hence the future residual of the normalized rational ghost $-p((2k-1)h-1)/h^2$ has raw Laurent integer coefficients. Subsequent raw integral corrections preserve this property, and involutivity makes every least residual anti-bar. Thus the positive-part recursion used next has genuine Laurent input for every integer $k\ge0$, despite its initial rational ghost.

**Uniform quotient extraction.** Put $U_1=(0,0,0,-p((2k-1)h-1)/h^2)^T$ at layer $4k+1$, and set $U_i=\mathcal P(\sum_{r=1}^{\min(3,i-1)}B_{4k+i-r,r}\bar U_{i-r})$ for $i=2,3,4,5$. In the matrix formula of step 5.1 replace $\binom{8k+N}{r}_q$ by $\prod_{j=1}^r(zq^{N-j+1}-z^{-1}q^{-N+j-1})/(q^j-q^{-j})$; thus $z=q^{8k}$, and crossing a four-layer period replaces $z$ by $q^8z$. Write $k=3m+c$, $c=0,1,2$, and $x=q^{24m}$. Each residual is a finite Laurent polynomial in $x$ with rational $q,m$ coefficients. Polynomial division at infinity and removal of its constant term defines a $\mathbb Q(m)$-linear operator on these rational coefficients; on their Laurent sum it is exactly $\mathcal P$. Write each nonzero-$x$-power coefficient, after cancelling powers of $q$, as $N/D$ with $D(0)\ne0$. For positive $x$-powers the numerator is a polynomial with zero valuation at least $18$, and every negative-power coefficient has infinity degree at most $-18$; the finite bounds and denominator products are calculated below. Accordingly $q^{24am}N/D$ has zero constant at zero for $a>0,m\ge0$, and for $a<0$ its infinity degree is negative for all $m\ge0$, so contributes no polynomial part. If $a>0$ and $D\mid(q^{24}-1)^3$, put $u=q^{24}-1$ and $\rho=\operatorname{rem}_D(N(1+am\,u+am(am-1)u^2/2))$. The binomial expansion of $(1+u)^{am}$ is exact modulo $D$, including $m=0$ and $am=1$, because $u^3=0$ there. Thus $\rho=\operatorname{rem}_D(q^{24am}N)$, and Euclidean division gives the exact positive part $q^{24am}N/D-\rho/D+\rho(0)/D(0)$: the quotient's constant is $-\rho(0)/D(0)$, since the dividend vanishes at zero. For $x$-power zero, ordinary numerator/denominator division followed by constant removal applies, even if the coefficient has a pole at zero. These arguments justify extraction term by term, with no specialization at a root and no missing small-$m$ case.

**The finite all-parameter identity.** The following quotient/remainder identities result from substitution in the explicit matrices of step 5.1 and the extraction rule of step 6.1. Let $H=(q-1)(q+1)$, $J=q^2+1$, $K=q^4+1$, and $L=(q^2-q+1)(q^2+q+1)$. For residual layers $i=2,3,4,5$ respectively, the common denominators after removing powers of $q$ divide $HJK^2$, $H^2J^2K^2$, $H^3J^2K^2L$, and $H^3J^3K^2L$; the least positive-$x$-power zero valuations are respectively $18+16c,21+16c,22+16c,27+16c$, and the greatest negative-$x$-power infinity degrees are their negatives. All factors $H,J,K,L$ divide $q^{24}-1$, with their distinct cyclotomic factors pairwise relatively prime, and the displayed exponents are at most three; hence each listed denominator divides $(q^{24}-1)^3$. To obtain these identities form $T_{t,r}$ from its matching pairs, multiply on the two sides by $D_{t+r}^{-1},D_t$, collect powers of $x$, and for each positive power replace its remainder by the three-term polynomial of step 6.1; collect again after each of the four layers. The scalar $U_{5,LL}-hU_{5,LH}+hU_{5,HL}-h^2U_{5,HH}$ then has the following coefficients of $ph,p$, with all other coefficients zero: for $c=0$, $(-(216m^3+216m^2+66m+6),36m^2+30m+6)$; for $c=1$, $(-(216m^3+432m^2+282m+60),36m^2+54m+20)$; for $c=2$, $(-(216m^3+648m^2+642m+210),36m^2+78m+42)$. These are finite rational-function identities, verified by the indicated polynomial divisions; the formulas above specify every input and operation. Substitution of $k=3m+c$ in the three output pairs gives exactly $-(2k+2)(2k+3)p((2k+1)h-1)$. Since the extraction bounds include $m=0$, this proves the cycle identity for every $k\ge0$.

**Factorial invariant and nonzero endpoint.** Apply step 7.1 to step 4.1, using only linearity under the integer multiplier $a_k$. Starting with $a_0=1$, the scalar multiplier satisfies $a_{k+1}=-(2k+2)(2k+3)a_k$, hence $a_k=(-1)^k(2k+1)!$ and $P-2hQ-h^2R=a_kp((2k-1)h-1)$ at every odd layer $4k+1$. Modulo $q^4+1$, $h=0$ and $-p=q^3-q$, so the first coordinate $P$ has remainder $a_k(q^3-q)$. Its divisor is monic and the displayed nonzero remainder has smaller degree. This proves nonvanishing of every odd endpoint in the coefficient family.

**Identification with all finite cuts and conclusion.** For any fixed $J$, raw coordinate projection of the layerwise family is a finite vector: only finitely many raw states have both indices at most $J$. Step 2.1 shows that each coefficient equation projects to its cut equation; the seed and positive-polynomial corrections project as well. Step 1.1 therefore identifies this vector with $g^{(J)}$. In particular all retained odd endpoints have the formula from step 8.1. The largest odd index at most $J$ is $J$ or $J-1$, giving the claimed escaping support in every cut. The finite projection comparison was proved with the omitted outgoing shear, so no full-formal/cut identification has been assumed. Every parameter, basis and finite calculation is specified, and no choice is used.

citations.quote:
Fix $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ and the crystal limiting ring $A_0\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ of [[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]], and put $A_\infty:=\psi(A_0)$, the image of $A_0$ under the semilinear involution $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, i.e. the ring of rational functions regular at $q=\infty$; $A_0$ and $A_\infty$ are the rational local rings at $0$ and at infinity, and the integral affine chart coordinate rings are $\mathbb Z[q]$ and $\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]$.

Let $M$ be one of $U_q^-$ or $V(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$ for $\lambda\in P^+$. Equip $M$ with the bar involution $\psi$ of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]]: on $U_q^-$ the semilinear algebra involution with $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(F_i)=F_i$, $\psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$; on $V(\lambda)$ the induced semilinear involution determined by $Pv_\lambda\mapsto\psi(P)v_\lambda$, well defined by the highest-module presentation: its negative-half kernel is $\sum_iU_q^-F_i^{\lambda(h_i)+1}$, preserved by $\psi$ because every $F_i$ is fixed ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]). Equivalently the full highest-vector relations are bar stable: $E_i$ is fixed, the singular divided powers are fixed, and $\psi(K_h-q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle})=-q^{-\langle\lambda,h\rangle}K_{-h}(K_h-q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle})$. Hence the quotient involution is compatible with the algebra action and fixes $v_\lambda$. Let $M_A\subseteq M$ be the divided-power integral form: $M_A=U_A^-$ for $M=U_q^-$, and $M_A=V_A(\lambda):=U_A^-v_\lambda$ for $M=V(\lambda)$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]); both are $\psi$-stable. Let $L$ be the Kashiwara crystal lattice of $M$ over $A_0$: $L=\mathcal L(\infty)$ for $U_q^-$ and $L=\mathcal L(\lambda)$ for $V(\lambda)$ ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]]).

Define the **bar lattice** $L^-:=\psi(L)$, an $A_\infty$-submodule of $M$, and the **balanced part** $E:=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$.

The definition keeps three structures on the same $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space strictly separate: the $A$-module $M_A$, which is not assumed free and not claimed to be contained in $L$; the free $A_0$-module $L$; and the free $A_\infty$-module $L^-$. No equality $L^-=L$, no inclusion $M_A\subseteq L$, no freeness of $M_A$ and no identification $E=M_A$ are asserted; freeness is a conclusion of the balanced-triple construction on this page, whereas $E$ is a $\mathbb Z$-module of global lifts and is not equal to the Laurent lattice $M_A$. The bar lattice is not the form-dual (upper) lattice, which is defined later on this page. The intersections $M_A\cap L$ and $M_A\cap L^-$ are respectively $\mathbb Z[q]$- and $\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]$-modules, generally not $A$-modules. The balanced part $E$ is a $\mathbb Z$-module; its Laurent extension $A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E$ is the full integral module once globalization is proved.

More generally a **based integrable module** $(M,B)$ here means exactly: $B$ is a homogeneous field basis; $M_A=\bigoplus_bAb$ is $U_A$-stable; the semilinear involution fixing $B$ is compatible with the algebra action; and $L_0=\bigoplus_bA_0b$ with residue $B$ is a crystal local basis at $0$. These are the four conditions of Lusztig 27.1.2(a)–(d) after the transport $v=q^{-1}$, together with the integrable extension used by Bao–Wang. Such data do not automatically imply an integral $\Theta$-action on an arbitrary based pair. A **based subobject** is a $U$-submodule spanned by a subset of $B$; a **based quotient** is its quotient with the complementary basis images. Based morphisms send $B$ to the target basis or to $0$, and have kernels spanned by the killed basis subset. These exact integral and bar-compatible maps, not arbitrary field summands, are used in tensor inheritance.

Use the actual periodic based $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ module and its finite cuts of [[lem-two-cyclotomic-shears-give-a-periodic-integrable-based-sl-two-chain]]. Thus $n_{2k}=8k+2$, $n_{2k+1}=8k+4$, $p=q+q^{-1}$, $h=q^2+q^{-2}$, and $M^{(J)}$ keeps constituents $0,\ldots,J$ and shears only at indices less than $J$. On $(M^{(J)})^{\otimes2}$ let $\Psi_J=\Theta(\psi\otimes\psi)$ be the actual rank-one tensor bar, and put $e^{(J)}=b_{0,0}\otimes b_{0,2}$. Every sum and vector here is algebraic.

For each $J\ge1$, there is a unique $\Psi_J$-fixed vector $g^{(J)}$ with seed coefficient $1$ and strictly increasing first-weight corrections in $q\mathbb Z[q]$. For every odd $j=2k+1\le J$, its coefficient $F_j(q)$ at $b_{j,0}\otimes b_{j,n_j}$ is independent of $J$ and satisfies

$$F_{2k+1}(q)\equiv(-1)^k(2k+1)!(q^3-q)\pmod{q^4+1}.$$

In particular this coefficient is nonzero. Every cut $J\ge1$ therefore has a nonzero corrected coordinate with constituent index at least $J-1$. For $L\ge J$, retaining the raw coordinates with both indices at most $J$ sends $g^{(L)}$ exactly to $g^{(J)}$, including at the last retained constituent where its outgoing shear has been omitted. No choice assumption is used.

In the same positive-first/negative-second completion $\widehat C$ of [[def-root-height-completion-for-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiners]], let $\Theta=\sum_\nu\Theta_\nu$ be the unique normalized bar-coproduct intertwiner of [[thm-the-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiner-exists-and-is-unique]]. Then:

(i) $\Theta^{-1}=\overline\Theta=(\psi\otimes\psi)(\Theta)$, the inverse being taken in the root-height convolution algebra of $\widehat C$ and not switching the positive and negative tensor order;

(ii) for every $\nu$ the exact threefold identities hold:
$$(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{23}(1\otimes K_{-\eta}\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{13},$$
$$(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{12}(1\otimes K_\eta\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{13},$$
with subscripts denoting tensor positions and $\Theta_{\nu'}=0$ when $\nu'\notin Q_+$;

(iii) the two normalized tensor-bar compositions satisfy the field cocycle identity
$$((\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Theta)\Theta_{12}=((\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Theta)\Theta_{23},$$
coefficientwise in the transported source completion and on every vector for which the iterated actions are finite;

(iv) the bar-coproduct counterpart needed for the cocycle is
$$(\mathrm{id}\otimes\overline\Delta)\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{13}(1\otimes K_{-\gamma}\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{12}.$$

Removing the normalization $\Theta_0=1$ permits arbitrary scalar multiples of the same linear intertwiner equation, so normalization is essential for uniqueness; no integrality of coefficients and no uncontrolled infinite evaluation is asserted.

derivations.claim: **A genuine algebraic integral tensor bar.** Each raw vector occupies finitely many finite standard divided strings, so only finitely many divided raising degrees in [F3] can act on its first factor. The evaluated tensor bar is therefore algebraic and finite column. Its coefficients are integral because the scalar in [F3] lies in $A$ and the actual factor lattices are divided-power stable. Unitarity makes it an involution, hence $\Psi(T_A)=T_A$. Degree zero is the identity and every other degree strictly raises first weight; the homogeneous shears preserve that weight. These properties hold in the actual four-axiom integrable finite-type module of [F1], without upper-cone bounds or completion.

**Every element of the natural intersection is fixed.** Put $E=T_A\cap T_0\cap\Psi(T_0)$. If $g\in E$, then both $g$ and $\Psi g$ belong to $T_A\cap T_0$: integral stability is step 1.1, and $g\in\Psi(T_0)$ implies $\Psi g\in T_0$. Thus $w=\Psi g-g$ has finite raw coefficients in $\mathbb Z[q]$ and satisfies $\Psi w=-w$. If $w\ne0$, choose the least first weight among its finitely many nonzero raw coordinates. Strict transfer cannot enter this weight from another nonzero coordinate, so each coefficient $s(q)$ there satisfies $s(q^{-1})=-s(q)$. A polynomial satisfying this equation has no positive degree, hence is constant; then $2s=0$ over $\mathbb Z$ forces $s=0$, a contradiction. Therefore every $g\in E$ is bar fixed. This does not assume that the tensor bar preserves the zero chart.

**The seed has no finite lift.** Let $e=b_{0,0}\otimes b_{0,2}$, of total weight zero and first weight two. Suppose $g\in E$ maps to its residue. By [F1], $g-e$ has finite coefficients in $q\mathbb Z[q]$. Project to total weight zero, which preserves $T_A,T_0,\Psi(T_0)$ and the seed residue because the bar preserves total weight; step 2.1 makes this projection fixed. For any cut $J$ exceeding its maximal constituent index by two, [F2] projects it to a cut fixed vector with the same seed residue and positive-polynomial correction coefficients. Such a cut vector has no correction at first weights below or equal to the seed: at its least first weight, fixedness forces polynomial coefficients to be constants, and the prescribed residue eliminates every lower coordinate and every other seed-weight coordinate. Repeating this within the finitely many lower weights proves the required triangular normalization. Finite-cut uniqueness in [F2] therefore identifies the projection with $g^{(J)}$. But the projection has no coordinate beyond the finite support of $g$, whereas [F2] gives a nonzero coordinate with index at least $J-1$. This contradiction proves that the seed residue is absent from the image of the natural map.

**Failure of unrestricted globalization.** The explicit natural integral reduction map is not surjective, and there is no algebraic normalized bar-fixed lift of $e$ in its raw integral zero chart. The two factors satisfy all four based axioms, are integrable and are of finite Cartan type; their actual tensor bar is finite, integral, triangular and involutive by step 1.1. Thus those hypotheses do not imply unrestricted finite supported tensor globalization or an integral balanced tensor triple. No assertion concerns bounded highest/lowest constructions, completion, or the finite-dimensional balanced-triple theorem.
